standing: OURS: a labelled decision record for the bounded, offline, review-only A05 assembly experiment Christian authorized in Christian's second reply of 5 November 2026. It is not a knowledge file, not a configuration step (the architecture has none: Steps 3-5 are held), not served, and not an authorization. Every value states how it reached the activity and which of Christian's six classes it falls in; values Christian's words do not state are ILLUSTRATIVE, OURS or UNRESOLVED. Nothing on the live route or the checked pathway reads this file.

gameProblemScope.idResolution: OURS: Christian's 5 November words name the Game Problems (Create Space, Exploit Space); the ids are the ones Christian's 3 November words name beside the same names, and the ones the Stage 1/2 resolution returns. The assembly fails closed if the resolution's ids differ, or if the names of the ids it returns are not in Christian's scope words.
gameProblemScope.note: The Game Problems are decided by the Stage 1/2 computation, whose trace stays the decisive record: Christian's scoped ruling filed as RUL-E1-A05 for the Stage 1 demonstration (scope STAGE1_DEVELOPMENT_DEMONSTRATION), continued by D1-4NOV, read because the planning model's Engine Translation for this goal is unpopulated. Christian's 5 November words set the scope this experiment uses (printed as scope set by, never decisive); they are not filed as a second scoped translation.

experimentPurpose.quote: The purpose is to determine whether the existing knowledge-grounded architecture can generate one complete, coherent, coach-readable activity while accurately preserving the authority and limitations of every design decision.

acceptance.quote: Can Challenge Point construct a complete, representative Progress the Attack activity using reusable, authorized knowledge, without requiring a fully authored activity-specific version?

caveat.quote: Please retain the ordinary kickoff as an acceptable provisional option for the current prototype, but do not promote it as a demonstrated method of restoring organized defensive relationships.

futureFeedbackQuestion.quote: Are players becoming more capable of finding functional solutions as the game changes?

lawsPrinciple.quote: The normal Laws of the Game should apply by default wherever they are applicable, unless an activity introduces an explicit, knowledge-authorized modification.

diagram.quote: The immediate understanding of the activity: learning purpose, one-sentence game description, basic parameters, essential scoring objectives, and a simple diagram.

rulings.decision: Purpose of the authorized experiment
rulings.subject: what the bounded experiment is to determine
words: The purpose is to determine whether the existing knowledge-grounded architecture can generate one complete, coherent, coach-readable activity while accurately preserving the authority and limitations of every design decision.

rulings.decision: Reconcile with the A05 assessment and reuse first
rulings.subject: reconciliation and reuse before implementation
words: Please first reconcile this assignment with your separate A05 assessment and identify any existing work that can be reused. I don't want duplicated implementation.

rulings.decision: Illustrative values permitted for the offline prototype
rulings.subject: values no knowledge authorizes
words: Where a choice cannot be authorized, an illustrative value may be used for this offline prototype if clearly labeled and kept outside production selection authority.

rulings.decision: Game Form alternatives (Deliverable C)
rulings.subject: GF2 illustrative; GF3 and GF7 visible, unranked
words: GF2 may be used as an illustrative configuration for this experiment.
GF3 and GF7 must remain visible as compatible alternatives without an invented ranking.
The selected form should not be presented as demonstrably superior merely because it is the one assembled.

rulings.decision: Game Form alternatives (first reply of 5 November)
rulings.subject: GF2 as an illustrative choice; the scale assessment across all three forms
words: For GF2, GF3, and GF7, the engine should continue preserving the compatible alternatives without manufacturing a preference.
Using GF2 for a review prototype is acceptable when explicitly described as an illustrative choice, not a justified selection over the other forms.
The proposed representative-scale assessment should apply to all three as knowledge permits, but it should not be used to invent a new ranking.

rulings.decision: A05 Game Problem translation (section 8)
rulings.subject: Create Space primary, Exploit Space secondary, within a scoped circumstance
scopeWords: within the scoped circumstance of progressing against organized opposition
words: Create Space remains the primary Game Problem and Exploit Space a secondary consideration within the scoped circumstance of progressing against organized opposition.
That is not yet an unconditional production translation for every A05 situation.
Please identify the smallest authoritative knowledge decision required to establish the appropriate scope.

rulings.decision: A05 Game Problem translation (first reply of 5 November)
rulings.subject: a scoped review interpretation; a possible mismatch to be flagged eventually; no switching
scopeWords: This remains a scoped review interpretation
specifically within the circumstance of progressing against organized opposition
words: I continue to support Create Space as A05's primary Game Problem, with Exploit Space as a secondary consideration, specifically within the circumstance of progressing against organized opposition.
This remains a scoped review interpretation rather than an unconditional mapping for every Progress the Attack situation.
If sufficient usable space already exists, the engine should eventually flag the possible mismatch between the described situation and the selected Game Problem.
It should not automatically switch Game Problems yet.

rulings.decision: Gain Access stays a candidate
rulings.subject: the candidate Game Problem relationship
words: Gain Access remains a candidate relationship, not an approved addition.

rulings.decision: Attack Development scoring source (section 8)
rulings.subject: the 13 September wording beside the workbook entry; the starting condition kept unresolved
words: Please provide the original September 13 wording alongside the current workbook entry, specifically the clause introduced with "for example" in the original approval.
We need to preserve the source's intended meaning rather than allowing transcription punctuation to turn an example into an exclusive definition.
Also retain the unresolved question of how the attack's starting condition should influence scoring or configuration.
Do not silently remove that condition by transferring it into the coach's observational emphasis.

rulings.decision: Decision 4: area-per-player definitions
rulings.subject: every dimensional reference states what it counts and includes
words: Every dimensional reference should explicitly identify whether goalkeepers are counted and whether end zones or other functional areas are included.
Where relevant, distinguish total playable area from the regions in which the principal interactions occur.
I am not authorizing canonical dimensional ranges or a production sizing algorithm.

rulings.decision: What the experiment can and cannot show
rulings.subject: coach-readability, tests and generated rationale are not evidence of ecological effectiveness
words: However, coach-readability does not establish that the design is ecologically validated.
As before, passing engineering tests should not be presented as proof of representative learning effectiveness.
The agents must not invent missing knowledge or present their generated rationale as evidence of ecological effectiveness.

rulings.decision: Three contrasting hypothetical scenarios (Deliverable E)
rulings.subject: the circumstances the activity is tested against (hypothetical, not rulings)
words: Organized opposition meaningfully restricts usable attacking space.
Sufficient usable space already exists, making exploitation potentially more immediate than creation.
Information about defensive organization and available opportunities is insufficient.

rulings.decision: What the system must do and not do in the scenarios (Deliverable E)
rulings.subject: preserve the distinction; report uncertainty; no automatic change of the primary and no width recommendation on unsupported assumptions
words: The system should preserve the distinction between Create Space and Exploit Space and report uncertainty where the relevant circumstances are unknown.
It should not automatically change the primary Game Problem or recommend width changes on unsupported assumptions.

rulings.decision: What the assembled activity includes (Deliverable A)
rulings.subject: the nine parts of the complete coach-readable activity
words: Assemble one A05 activity using the available Game Form and approved knowledge wherever possible.
Learning purpose and relevant Game Problems.
Game Form and player configuration.
Playing dimensions and layout.
Setup and starting conditions.
Rules and interaction regulations.
Scoring and consequences.
Restarts and continuous-play behavior.
Coach-facing instructions and appropriate observation guidance.
A clear explanation of the design rationale.
The activity should be complete enough that a coach could understand and run it.

rulings.decision: Christian's six classes for every material design choice (Deliverable B)
rulings.subject: what each material design choice follows from, in Christian's order; the report places every value in one of them
words: For every material design choice, identify whether it follows from:
Approved canonical knowledge.
An explicit scoped ruling.
Candidate or provisional knowledge.
A stated test assumption.
An illustrative configuration choice.
An unsupported or unresolved relationship.

rulings.decision: The bounds of the authorization
rulings.subject: a narrow authorization; not production, broad Stage 2, canonical changes or adaptive functionality
words: This is a narrow authorization to implement and test the isolated assembly pathway necessary for that demonstration.
It is not authorization for production deployment, broad Stage 2 implementation, canonical library changes, or new adaptive functionality.

rulings.decision: Representative-suitability assessment (Deliverable D)
rulings.subject: the six properties, scale, and what remains unknown
words: Please assess whether the assembled activity retains meaningful opposition, direction, information, consequences, adaptive player roles, and multiple functional solutions.
Also examine whether its game scale can reasonably represent the intended problem and what remains unknown about exposure frequency, distribution, and challenge.
Do not require the activity to contain an additional constraint simply to differentiate it from a generic game.

rulings.decision: Scale and the absence of added constraints
rulings.subject: no automatic preference for small-sided games; a simple Game Form may suffice if justified
words: Challenge Point should not automatically prefer small-sided games.
Likewise, the absence of additional constraints should not be considered a design failure.
A simple Game Form may be the best configuration if there is sufficient knowledge to justify its suitability.

rulings.decision: A question preserved for future coach feedback
rulings.subject: the question is preserved for a future feedback experience, not implemented now
scopeWords: This is a future feedback direction
words: For our eventual lightweight coach-feedback experience, I'd like to preserve this question:
Are players becoming more capable of finding functional solutions as the game changes?
This is a future feedback direction, not a request to implement learning analytics now.

rulings.decision: Composite Runtime Specification (section 8)
rulings.subject: the primary-led direction; draft wording kept; missing documents not reconstructed
words: The primary Game Problem should govern the learning intention, while secondary requirements and their provenance remain visible.
A stronger secondary requirement must not be automatically promoted, nor silently discarded.
Please retain the proposed section 7 and section 9 clarification as draft wording until the source specification and CAR Matrix are reconciled.

words: These unresolved items should be shown explicitly in the experiment rather than treated as reasons to invent decisions or prevent all review-only assembly.

rulings.subject: the kickoff for the current prototype; not a method of restoring organized defence
words: Please retain the ordinary kickoff as an acceptable provisional option for the current prototype, but do not promote it as a demonstrated method of restoring organized defensive relationships.

rulings.decision: Continuous play through turnovers
rulings.subject: play continues through changes of possession
scopeWords: whenever doing so supports the intended representative problem
words: I favor preserving continuous play through turnovers whenever doing so supports the intended representative problem.

rulings.subject: no approved basis for 6v6, 40 x 30 m; width and length not interchangeable
words: Although those dimensions may be reasonable for a review prototype, we currently have no approved basis for treating them as particularly appropriate for A05.
Likewise, width and length should not be treated as interchangeable simply because total area remains constant.
For now, A05's dimensions remain provisional, and W-H1/W-H2 remain test-only hypotheses.

rulings.subject: suitability unverified where the knowledge does not support adding nothing
words: I would not require a feature that differentiates the design from a generic game.
A knowledge-supported decision to add nothing should be considered a valid design decision.
Where the knowledge doesn't support that conclusion, the system should report that suitability remains unverified.

They should not become production selection criteria or be interpreted as evidence of learning simply because the intended situation appears.

words: If the original approval used "for example" before the final clause, then that clause should retain its status as an example rather than becoming an exclusive definition through transcription punctuation.
I don't want to authorize a canonical amendment until we've verified the exact source text and its interpretation.
Likewise, the condition concerning the attack's starting circumstances should not disappear into an observational emphasis if doing so removes a meaningful part of the approved context.

rulings.decision: A coach-served ball when the ball leaves play
rulings.subject: a way to keep game flow; not equivalent to a live turnover; does not create organized opposition
words: When the ball leaves play, a coach quickly serving a new ball can be an effective way to maintain game flow, energy, and the frequency of meaningful opportunities.
That may be particularly helpful when traditional restarts introduce unnecessary dead time.
However, a coach-served ball should not automatically be treated as equivalent to a live turnover, nor should we assume that it creates organized opposition.

words: I would also avoid requiring fixed positions, waiting periods, or predetermined movement sequences simply to guarantee a defensive organization.

words: I don't want to authorize automatic switching between those Game Problems yet.

This should remain a reusable reasoning requirement, not an A05-specific exception.

rulings.decision: Observation criteria, provisionally approved
rulings.subject: three categories; both situations legitimate; no threshold
words: Observation criteria — Provisionally approved

During transition: The team scores before the opposition has recovered its organization.
Uncertain: The coach cannot confidently distinguish the situation.

I would not set a required percentage or threshold before gathering field evidence.

rulings.decision: Default soccer rules (a standing principle)
rulings.subject: the normal Laws by default; only departures defined; adaptations identified
words: The normal Laws of the Game should apply by default wherever they are applicable, unless an activity introduces an explicit, knowledge-authorized modification.
For example, normal rules should govern goalkeeper handling, fouls, and own goals unless the activity deliberately changes them.

Where a normal law cannot apply directly because of the modified field, scoring structure, or game format, the system should identify the relevant adaptation rather than silently assume conventional conditions exist.
The governing principle is to inherit established sport rules and explicitly define only the necessary departures.

rulings.decision: Organized defence: working definition
rulings.subject: a functional definition of an organized defence
words: A defense is functionally organized when its players have sufficiently coordinated relationships to challenge progression, provide mutual support, and adapt collectively to the attacking team's changing opportunities.

laws.reason: The ordinary kickoff at the start and after a point (Christian's provisional option); the centre mark and halfway line it needs are marked (illustrative).
A stoppage the coach makes restarts with a dropped ball, as in the Laws; nothing departs from it.
No offside: Christian's provisional ruling, explicitly communicated.
There is no goalkeeper, so no goalkeeper handling; no player may handle the ball.
No goal stands at either end, so there is no penalty kick.

Free kicks as in the Laws; nothing departs from them. Review point (OURS): a free kick next to a target zone keeps the opponents 9.15 m from the ball, which can leave the zone empty for an immediate point; no rule is invented (listed in Part 3 as a known risk).

Throw-ins as in the Laws; nothing departs from them. Review point (OURS): a throw-in beside a target zone, to a teammate standing in it, could give an immediate point, although the Laws allow no goal straight from a throw-in; no rule is invented (listed in Part 3 as a known risk).

The goal kick restarts a ball over the end line but assumes a goal and its goal area; there is no goal here, so an adaptation is owed. The ILLUSTRATIVE end-line value stands in (the team defending the target zone at that end restarts from that end line), pending Christian's confirmation. Review point (OURS): the Laws keep opponents outside the penalty area until a goal kick is in play; nothing here does, and that end line is the back edge of the target zone the opponents attack, so an opponent standing in that zone who intercepts the restart and controls the ball there scores at once; no rule is invented (listed in Part 3 as a known risk).

The corner kick restarts a ball over the end line but assumes a goal with a corner area beside it; there is no goal here, so an adaptation is owed. A corner kick would also be taken inside a target zone, where a pass to a teammate could give an immediate point (review point, OURS). The same ILLUSTRATIVE end-line value stands in, pending Christian's confirmation.

properties.note: Two opposing teams with reciprocal objectives and continuous play are present by configuration; whether defenders can functionally influence attacking opportunities (Christian's 5 November wording) can be seen only in play.
Each team attacks a fixed target zone at one end.
Live opposition in one shared area keeps defensive organization, teammate positioning and emerging space as information; whether that information is representative can be seen only in play.
Points, turnovers that keep play live, and immediate attacks after a regain are consequences present by configuration.
Attacking and defending roles change with possession while target assignments stay fixed; whether players adapt can be seen only in play.
No rule removes a legal option and the event can be reached by a dribble or by receiving and controlling the ball in the zone; whether several solutions are functional can be seen only in play.

reviewPoints.statement: Attackers may wait inside the target zone for a pass: a risk Christian has seen in similar games (said of the build-out activity, 15 October). Applying it here is ours (OURS: CAUSAL HYPOTHESIS). No mechanism is imposed, as Christian's words ask; it bears on meaningful opposition and on multiple functional solutions, and is visible only in play.

A restart taken beside or inside a target zone could give an immediate point: a throw-in to a teammate standing in the zone; a free kick next to it, which keeps the opponents 9.15 m from the ball; a corner kick, were one taken. The Laws apply unchanged and no rule is invented; the end-line value has the team defending a target zone restart from its own end line, on the back edge of the zone its opponents attack; with no opponent distance added, an opponent standing in that zone who intercepts the restart and controls the ball there scores at once. Visible only in play.

openDecisions.question: May the illustrative end-line restart stand in this offline example? With it, when the ball goes over an end line, the team defending the target zone at that end restarts from that end line, so no restart is taken on the edge of the zone the restarting team attacks (a departure the Laws do not supply: their goal kick and corner kick assume a goal). With it, opponents may wait inside the target zone at that end, whose back edge is that end line, and score by intercepting the restart. Is that acceptable, or would you prefer a coach-served ball there ("a coach quickly serving a new ball can be an effective way to maintain game flow, energy, and the frequency of meaningful opportunities"), not treated as a live turnover?
